figures.caption: Figure 2: A schematic of a φ-t curve of a Redox Flow Battery (RFB) anolyte in galvanostatic discharge (blue curve) over the full discharge time-scale. δV is given as its initial slope (the cyan dashed line). The red emphatic region shows the kMC simulation potential (in purple), and δV is the slope of the potential obtained in the kMC simulation.

figures.caption: Figure 3: A schematic illustrating the kMC-LBM coupling workflow employed in this work.

Figure 4: (a) δV (in V/ns) obtained for various boundary layer concentrations of MV (in M) (b) 2D slices of snapshots of kMC simulations of 1 M MV (top) and 0.05 M MV (bottom) viewed along their Debye length (LD). Heatmaps of δV (in V/ns) interpolated for various boundary layer concentrations of MV (in x-axis) and supporting electrolyte concentrations of (c) NaCl and (d) K2SO4 in the y-axes. The concentrations are represented with “[]”, in units of mol/L.

Figure 5: Graph of LBM-calculated permeabilities (in 10-10 m2) in the y-axis versus SSA (in m-1) in X-axis for the five microstructures considered, plotted as scatters with different shapes and colours, as in the legend at top-right, and connected by a dotted line to help visualizing the trend. Next to each point, there is the respective 3D carbon felt electrode microstructure.
